identity.name: Tampere University tuition fee scholarship (50%) and early bird offer

verifiable_urls.kind: terms and conditions of Tampere University scholarships

records.description: Tampere University offers a limited number of partial scholarships and an early bird discount to support fee-paying students. The tuition fee scholarship covers 50% of the tuition fees for the programme duration and is awarded to exceptionally qualified applicants; in admission 2026 only nine were awarded across all bachelor's and master's programmes, and scholarships are not awarded in all programmes. The separate early bird offer gives every fee-paying student who has not received a scholarship a EUR 2,000 reduction on the first-year tuition if they accept and pay within three weeks.

official.program_type: Merit-based partial tuition fee scholarship, plus an automatic early bird tuition reduction
eligibility: Citizen of a country outside the EU, EEA and Switzerland, or otherwise liable to pay tuition fees
Study in a Tampere University bachelor's or master's programme taught in English
Merited, high-achieving and motivated fee-paying student
Scholarships are not available in the open university route or transfer applications
Scholarships are not awarded in all programmes
benefits: Tampere University tuition fee scholarship: 50% of the tuition fees for the programme duration
Early bird offer: EUR 2,000 reduction on the programme tuition fee during the first year of studies
Graduation Scholarship: EUR 2,000 reduction on the tuition fee for the first year of master's studies for students who complete a Tampere University bachelor's degree within three academic years
Tuition fees for students admitted in 2027: EUR 10,000 in all bachelor's programmes and EUR 12,000 in all master's programmes
selection_criteria: Scholarships are awarded on the basis of academic overall assessment in which all application information and educational documents, as well as the scholarship application letter if applicable, are taken into consideration
The scholarship is an exclusive opportunity awarded to a limited number of the best-performing applicants
The decision on the scholarship is communicated together with information on admission
application_process: Apply for the scholarship as part of the application for admission during the application period for admission
Use the same online application used to apply for admission at Studyinfo.fi
All application information and educational documents submitted for admission are available to the admissions committee evaluating the scholarship application
The early bird offer is available without a separate application to fee-paying students who have not been awarded a tuition fee scholarship
Claim the early bird offer by accepting the offered study place and paying the reduced first-year tuition within three weeks (21 days) after receiving information on admission
official.duration: Tuition fee scholarship: for the programme duration. Early bird offer: valid only for the first year of studies.
key_dates: Scholarship request: within the admission application period for the programme
Early bird offer: accept and pay within three weeks (21 days) after receiving information on admission
Bachelor's applicants admitted from the waiting list: the early bird offer is only available if three or more weeks remain to the deadline for accepting the study place

deadlines.label: Early bird offer payment window
deadlines.date_display: within three weeks (21 days) after receiving information on admission
deadlines.note: Relative deadline, not a fixed calendar date. Accept the study place and pay the reduced first-year tuition within three weeks of the admission information.

verification.deadline_note: Tampere University publishes no fixed scholarship calendar. The scholarship is requested inside the admission application, so it follows the programme's admission application period; the only stated deadline is the three-week window for the early bird offer after admission information is received.
verification.application_cycle: Per admission intake; the page refers to scholarships available at admission in 2027 and cites admission 2026 award numbers
verification.tuition_coverage_note: The tuition fee scholarship covers 50% of the tuition fees for the programme duration. The page does not describe any living cost support; it states that all students must fund their living costs themselves.
verification.english_requirement: The scholarship attaches to English-taught bachelor's and master's programmes for which non-EU/EEA/Swiss students pay tuition. No scholarship-specific English score is published on this page.

Scholarships are not available through the open university route or transfer applications.

applicant_utility.description: The realistic expectation-setting here is brutal and useful: nine tuition fee scholarships across every bachelor's and master's programme in a whole admission year, with some programmes awarding none at all. That makes the EUR 2,000 early bird offer the award most applicants will actually get - and it is automatic, requiring only that you accept and pay within three weeks. The tuition fee scholarship, by contrast, rides entirely on your admission application, so the practical advice is to treat the admission materials as scholarship materials and not to plan your finances around a 50% waiver you are unlikely to receive.
eligibility_tips: You must be liable for tuition fees: a citizen of a country outside the EU, EEA and Switzerland, or otherwise fee-liable. EU/EEA/Swiss citizens are outside the scheme by definition.

Scholarships attach to English-taught bachelor's and master's programmes only, and are unavailable via the open university route or transfer applications - a common route for international students that is explicitly excluded.
The Graduation Scholarship is a separate, automatic path: complete a Tampere University bachelor's degree within three academic years and you get EUR 2,000 off your first master's year.
application_tips: Request the scholarship inside the Studyinfo.fi admission application. There is no separate form, so the request is a box to tick rather than a document to prepare.

Because the committee sees the same materials as admissions, put your best evidence there - Tampere explicitly includes all application information and educational documents in the scholarship assessment.
Protect the early bird offer: keep EUR 2,000 accessible in the three weeks after your admission information, because the reduced first-year fee must be paid in that window.
If your programme awards no scholarships at all, you will not know until the admission decision - so keep an external funding plan alive until then.
documents: Admission application documents at Studyinfo.fi, which double as the scholarship application.
A scholarship application letter where the programme requires one.
mistakes_to_avoid: Assuming the 50% scholarship is the default. It is awarded to a small number of the best-performing applicants and not in every programme.
Missing the three-week early bird window by waiting for funds to arrive. The offer is lost and the full first-year fee stands.
Applying through the open university route or as a transfer applicant hoping for a scholarship - neither is eligible.
Counting the scholarship towards living costs. Tampere states plainly that all students must fund living costs themselves and these are not included in the tuition fee.
applicant_utility.deadline_notes: Tampere publishes no scholarship calendar at all: the scholarship request lives inside the admission application period, so the deadline you must watch is your programme's admission deadline at Studyinfo.fi, not a scholarship date. The single published deadline is the three-week early bird payment window after admission information, which also applies to waiting-list bachelor's applicants only if three or more weeks remain to their acceptance deadline. Decisions on the scholarship arrive together with the admission decision, so there is no separate notification date to plan around.

identity.name: Åbo Akademi University tuition fee scholarship - early commitment offer and second-year reduction

verifiable_urls.kind: tuition fee scholarships for master's students

records.description: For students admitted to Åbo Akademi University international master's programmes from the autumn of 2026 onwards, the university replaced its previous 100% and 80% tuition waiver scheme with an early commitment offer. Fee-liable admitted students receive a EUR 4,000 discount, leaving EUR 8,000 for the first academic year, provided they accept their study place and pay the tuition fee within the deadline specified in their admissions letter. All admitted students are awarded a EUR 4,000 tuition fee reduction in the second year, also leaving EUR 8,000, with no separate application required.

official.program_type: Tuition fee discount awarded on admission, continued automatically in year two
eligibility: Admitted to an Åbo Akademi University international master's degree programme
Liable to pay a tuition fee - if you are exempted from paying tuition fees you are not eligible for the scholarship
Studies starting in the autumn of 2026 or later
Early commitment offer: accept the study place and pay the tuition fee within the deadline specified in the admissions letter
Scholarships are granted only for the first two years of study at ÅAU
Decisions regarding all scholarships are final and may not be appealed
benefits: Early commitment offer: EUR 4,000 discount in the first academic year, leaving a remaining tuition fee of EUR 8,000
Second year: EUR 4,000 tuition fee reduction for all admitted students, leaving EUR 8,000
If the early commitment offer is not claimed, admitted students must pay the full amount of EUR 12,000
The former 100% and 80% tuition fee waiver scheme applies only to students admitted in 2025 or earlier
selection_criteria: The 100% Tuition Fee Scholarship for students admitted in 2025 or earlier was awarded 1 per programme

The 80% Tuition Fee Scholarship for students admitted in 2025 or earlier was granted to all admitted applicants liable to pay tuition fees who had not received a 100% waiver, with no application needed
For 2026 onwards the early commitment offer is a claimable entitlement rather than a competitive award
application_process: Apply to an international master's degree programme through the normal application process
Claim the early commitment offer by accepting the study place and paying the tuition fee within the deadline specified in the admissions letter
No separate application is needed for the second year reduction, which is awarded to all admitted students
All students remain entitled to apply for other Åbo Akademi student scholarships throughout their study period
official.duration: Tuition fee scholarships are granted only for the first two years of study at Åbo Akademi University
key_dates: Early commitment offer: accept and pay within the deadline specified in the admissions letter
Second-year reduction: automatic, no separate application or deadline

deadlines.date_display: the deadline specified in the admissions letter
deadlines.note: Åbo Akademi does not publish a calendar date. The deadline is individually set in each admitted student's admissions letter, and students who miss it must pay the full EUR 12,000.

verification.deadline_note: No published calendar deadline. The first-year early commitment offer must be claimed within the deadline stated in the admissions letter; the second-year reduction requires no action and has no deadline.
verification.application_cycle: For students admitted for studies starting in the autumn of 2026 or later; the former 100%/80% waiver scheme is closed to 2026 and later admissions
verification.tuition_coverage_note: The awards are tuition fee discounts only. Åbo Akademi describes them as reductions in tuition fees and publishes no living cost, travel or insurance support on this page.
verification.english_requirement: Programme-level English language requirements apply for international master's programmes; Åbo Akademi publishes them on a separate language requirements page rather than on the scholarship page.
verification.status_note: The page presents the early commitment offer as the current scheme for students admitted in autumn 2026 or later, and states explicitly that scholarships mentioned for students admitted earlier are not available to those admitted in 2026 or later.

applicant_utility.description: This is a payment-timing scheme, not a merit competition: the money is already allocated to every fee-liable admitted student, and the only way to lose it is to miss the deadline buried in your admissions letter. That makes it a EUR 4,000 reward for having cash ready at short notice and a EUR 4,000 penalty for hesitation, since students who do not claim the offer owe the full EUR 12,000. The second-year reduction is automatic and requires nothing, so your entire practical task is to read the letter carefully and move funds quickly.
eligibility_tips: You must be liable to pay tuition fees. Åbo Akademi states that students exempted from tuition are not eligible for the scholarship, so fee-exempt status removes the award entirely.

The scheme applies only to international master's degree programmes with studies starting in autumn 2026 or later. If you were admitted in 2025 or earlier, the old 100%/80% waiver rules apply instead.
Awards run for the first two years of study only - you will still need a funding plan for any third year or for living costs throughout.
application_tips: Read the admissions letter for the payment deadline as your first action. It is not a fixed university-wide date and it is the only thing standing between you and EUR 4,000.
Arrange the funds before the letter arrives. A bank transfer that takes a week to clear can quietly cost you the discount.
Do not look for a scholarship application form for the first year - there is none. Payment is the application.
Do nothing at all for the second year. Åbo Akademi states applicants do not need to apply separately and all admitted students receive the EUR 4,000 reduction.
documents: No scholarship documents. The evidence of claim is the tuition fee payment itself, made within the deadline in the admissions letter.
mistakes_to_avoid: Treating the admissions letter as a formality. The deadline inside it is the operative date, and missing it means paying the full EUR 12,000.
Assuming you can appeal. Åbo Akademi states decisions regarding all scholarships are final and may not be appealed.
Applying as a fee-exempt student, which is explicitly out of scope.
Expecting the award to help with living costs. It is a fee reduction only, and Turku living costs are entirely on you.
applicant_utility.deadline_notes: There is no published calendar deadline for either award. The first-year early commitment offer must be claimed within the deadline stated in your admissions letter, and the second-year reduction is automatic with no date attached. Because Åbo Akademi grants scholarships only for the first two years and decisions are final and unappealable, the practical advice is to secure the first payment on time and to plan independently for the remainder of your costs.
